content: The Muslim Brotherhood was founded in 1928 by Hassan al-Banna (d.1949 seated third from left). The Muslim Brotherhood was a revivalist organisation, it advocated a return to the Qurʾān and the Hadith as guidelines for a healthy modern Islamic society. The Brotherhood spread rapidly throughout Egypt, Sudan, Syria, Palestine, Lebanon, and North Africa. Although figures of Brotherhood membership are variable, it is estimated that at its height in the late 1940s it may have had some 500,000 members.
